content: PPT1, also referred to as palmitoyl-protein hydrolase 1, is an enzyme encoded by the PPT1 gene in humans. This enzyme belongs to the family of palmitoyl-protein thioesterases. It is a small glycoprotein that plays a critical role in the breakdown of lipid-modified proteins during lysosomal degradation. Specifically, PPT1 functions by removing thioester-linked fatty acyl groups, such as palmitate, from cysteine residues in proteins. Mutations or defects in the PPT1 gene are associated with a severe neurodegenerative disorder known as neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis type 1 (CLN1). This condition is characterized by the accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigments in neurons, leading to progressive neurological decline.
